items.name: S&P 500 (VFV + SPY)
items.street: Strategists are split: earnings are still growing, but the market is leaning on a handful of AI names while yields and oil stay high.
items.take: Crowd mood on the S&P 500 is about as gloomy as it gets, while the index itself has barely pulled back. Your VFV and SPY move together, so this is the sentiment that matters most for you.

bears: Capex of $195–205B this year has pushed free cash flow negative
Debt and equity raising to fund AI build-out
Chart broke support; some traders are calling for $250 if capex rises again
bulls: Google Cloud grew 82% last quarter with a $514B backlog
TPU chips are seen as a $100B+ opportunity and a challenge to Nvidia
Stock looks oversold (RSI near 30) at about 24x forward earnings
items.name: Alphabet
items.street: Strong Buy from 62 analysts; average target about $421–431, roughly a third above Friday's $317 close. Q3 consensus: revenue about $127.5B (+25%), EPS about $3.
items.take: The crowd is divided into two camps: a Cloud blowout sends it higher, a capex hike sends it lower. Your call is about $13 below its $330 strike, so the Oct 28 reaction matters a lot for its value.

bears: About $220B of capex this year weighs on free cash flow
Reports of GPUs sitting idle in warehouses feed bubble talk
Soft retail guidance and a disclosed founder share sale
bulls: AWS growth has sped up five quarters in a row, to 36.7% last quarter
AWS capacity is reported sold out through 2026
Stock is about 13% off its August high at about 24x next year's earnings
items.name: Amazon
items.street: Strong Buy from 60 analysts; average target about $331, about a third above Friday's $248 close. The number everyone is watching is AWS growth (30–35% expected).
items.take: Retail traders are more upbeat on Amazon than on Alphabet going into earnings. Your call is about $12 below its $260 strike; AWS growth vs. the 30–35% range is the swing factor.

mood.summary: Investors are nervous. The Fear & Greed index has sat in Extreme Fear for two weeks, and bearish individual investors outnumber bulls by about 9 points, well below the long-run norm. The S&P 500 fell for a second week and is about 2.5% off its Oct 6 record, while the Nasdaq is about 6% off after its worst day since June on Oct 22. Worries centre on AI spending, oil above $110 on Middle East tensions, and a possible Fed hike in December. Very fearful readings have often come before rebounds, but they don't say when.

trending.note: Board as of Sunday afternoon; prices are Friday's close. Why-it's-trending notes summarize the Stocktwits stream and the news it links to.

items.name: Summit Therapeutics
items.about: Biotech developing ivonescimab, a PD-1/VEGF cancer antibody it licenses from China's Akeso for the US, Europe and Japan.
items.why: Akeso presented ivonescimab data in bile duct cancer at the ESMO conference on Sunday: about a 25% lower risk of death than durvalumab, with median survival of 14.9 vs 12.1 months. The debate is how much a China-only interim result counts. The FDA decision on ivonescimab in EGFR-mutated lung cancer is due Nov 14.

items.name: Mattel
items.about: Toymaker behind Barbie, Hot Wheels and Fisher-Price.
items.why: Takeover pressure. Southeastern Asset Management is reportedly preparing a proxy fight to force a sale (per Semafor), and Authentic Brands Group has shown takeover interest. Chatter is split on whether management will engage; the stock fell 3.1% Friday.

items.name: Whirlpool
items.about: Appliance maker (Whirlpool, KitchenAid, Maytag).
items.why: Reports Q3 Monday after the close. Posts citing Zacks put consensus at about 78¢ a share, down roughly 63% from a year ago, on about $3.9B of revenue. The stock is down about 26% in three months on a weak housing market, and message volume is the highest on the board.

items.name: Natera
items.about: Genetic testing company: prenatal screening, transplant and cancer-recurrence blood tests.
items.why: Holding near its highs while the market sold off. Traders flagged large out-of-the-money January call purchases (about $1.9M in $400 calls and $1.3M in $460 calls). Two billing class-action settlements are also drawing posts.

items.name: AstraZeneca
items.about: UK-based drugmaker focused on cancer, rare disease and respiratory medicines.
items.why: ESMO cancer-conference news: Amgen's Imdelltra combined with AstraZeneca's Imfinzi cut the risk of death by 58% in a Phase 3 small-cell lung cancer trial (median survival 21.1 vs 12.7 months, as reported by CNBC). It also appears on weekend technical watchlists.

items.name: Vanguard Total Stock Market ETF
items.about: Holds essentially the entire US stock market in one fund.
items.why: A stand-in for overall market nerves heading into a heavy week: big-tech earnings, the Oct 27–28 Fed meeting and geopolitical headlines. Crowd mood on it is bearish.

items.name: Spotify
items.about: Music and podcast streaming platform.
items.why: Post-earnings follow-through: premium subscribers beat expectations by about 1 million and ad revenue growth sped up to 9%. Several analysts raised targets (Guggenheim to $650, Raymond James to $625), and chartists are calling a breakout.

items.name: Fundrise Innovation Fund
items.about: Listed fund holding stakes in private tech companies, including Anthropic.
items.why: Anthropic IPO speculation. Traders expect a filing soon, and VCX jumped 5.2% Friday. Posts say it trades at roughly a 15% premium to its asset value, which is drawing short-sellers as well as buyers.

items.name: Okta
items.about: Identity and login security software for companies.
items.why: Cybersecurity rally. After Thursday's tech sell-off, security stocks (CrowdStrike, Palo Alto, Zscaler, Okta) jumped Friday as AI-found software flaws made headlines, including a PHP vulnerability Palo Alto confirmed affects its products. Okta rose 5.8%.

items.name: FMC Corp
items.about: Crop-protection chemicals maker (insecticides, herbicides).
items.why: A heated bull-bear fight after the stock collapsed to about $5. An October update brought a roughly $650M write-down and a reset outlook. Bulls say 2026 is the bottom of the cycle and asset sales are paying down debt; bears warn of further dividend cuts or worse.

items.name: Charles Schwab
items.about: Largest US retail brokerage (Schwab and thinkorswim platforms).
items.why: Users posted about app and thinkorswim access problems late last week. There's also attention on record margin-loan balances at brokers, a sign of how much borrowed money is in the market.

items.name: Bitdeer Technologies
items.about: Bitcoin miner that designs its own mining chips and is pitching its sites for AI computing.
items.why: Fell 4.4% as bitcoin weakened. Holders argue the market ignores its chip business and AI data-centre plans; skeptics point to about $2B of debt against modest revenue.

items.name: CVS Health
items.about: Pharmacy chain, Aetna health insurer and pharmacy-benefit manager in one.
items.why: Climbed through October, then dipped Friday ahead of its Nov 4 earnings. Most posts are trade setups into the report, plus several class-action notices.

items.name: Centrus Energy
items.about: Supplies enriched uranium, including HALEU fuel for next-generation reactors.
items.why: Pulled back to about $100. Bulls point to a $4.5B backlog against a roughly $2B market value, heavy short interest and possible Energy Department contracts; earnings are around Nov 4 and some worry a Fed hike would hit it.

items.name: Visa
items.about: Global card-payments network.
items.why: Reports Tuesday after the close, sitting just below its yearly high. Options price about a ±3% move; it has beaten estimates in recent quarters but only rose after about half of them. Some posts flag cyberattack risk to payment networks.

items.name: Roblox
items.about: Online gaming platform where users build and play games.
items.why: Reports Q3 Thursday after the close. It guided bookings down 14–18% from a year ago after age-verification changes hurt engagement; Wedbush raised its target to $55 on better-than-feared user numbers. Shareholder suits over the age checks are also in the stream.

items.name: Wells Fargo
items.about: One of the four largest US banks.
items.why: Axios reported that major banks, including Wells Fargo, are detecting unauthorized third-party AI agents acting inside customer accounts. The stock is sitting on support near $81 after a mid-October earnings beat.

items.name: Intuit
items.about: Maker of TurboTax, QuickBooks and Credit Karma.
items.why: Down roughly 50% from its high on fears AI will disrupt tax and accounting software. Dip buyers argue about 13x forward earnings is cheap and money is rotating from AI hardware into profitable software; it fell 3.2% Friday.

items.name: Eli Lilly
items.about: Drugmaker behind the Mounjaro and Zepbound weight-loss and diabetes drugs.
items.why: Earnings Thursday morning after a record week. At ESMO it showed a 79% response rate for its new ovarian-cancer drug (an antibody-drug conjugate) and lung-cancer data for olomorasib. Stock-split hopes are a recurring thread.

items.name: Johnson & Johnson
items.about: Diversified healthcare company: drugs and medical devices.
items.why: ESMO prostate-cancer news: an early-stage drug, JNJ-6143, showed a 75% tumor response rate, and posts cite a larger trial cutting recurrence risk by 62%. It recently raised its full-year sales outlook to a $101.2B midpoint.
